question: Arrange the following rulers of the Sharqi dynasty in the chronological order.  (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Hussain Shah < Ibrahim Shah < Mubarak Shah < Mahmud Shah
Mahmud Shah < Hussain Shah < Mubarak Shah < Ibrahim Shah
Hussain Shah < Mubarak Shah < Ibrahim Shah < Mahmud Shah
Mubarak Shah < Ibrahim Shah < Mahmud Shah < Hussain Shah
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mubarak Shah

Explanation:
The Sharqi dynasty was founded by Malik Sarwar in 1394 AD, who assumed the title of Khwaja-i-Jahan. The correct chronological order of its major rulers is: Mubarak Shah (1399-1401) ruled first, followed by Ibrahim Shah (1401-1440), who had a long reign and promoted the Sharqi style of architecture. After him, Mahmud Shah (1440-1457) ascended the throne, and the last ruler was Hussain Shah (1457-1479), under whom the sultanate expanded and later ended after defeat by Bahlol Lodi.

☛ Under which ruler did the Sharqi empire expand? → Hussain Shah
☛ Who ended the Sharqi dynasty? → Bahlol Lodi (1479 AD)
☛ Which art did Ibrahim Shah promote? → Architecture (Sharqi style)
question_hi: शर्की वंश के निम्नलिखित शासकों को कालानुक्रमिक क्रम में व्यवस्थित करें। (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)

question: Under the reign of which of the following Mughal Emperors did Bahadur Shah attack Chittor? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Aurangzeb
Shah Jahan
Humayun
Babur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Humayun

Explanation:
Bahadur Shah (Sultan of Gujarat) attacked Chittor in 1535 during the reign of the Mughal Emperor Humayun. Humayun (1530-1540 and 1555-1556) was the second ruler of the Mughal Empire. At that time, Chittor was under the rule of Rana Sangram Singh (Rana Sanga), who sought help against Bahadur Shah's invasion. Although Humayun did not directly attack Chittor, the invasion occurred during his reign. Later, Humayun defeated Bahadur Shah and annexed Gujarat. This event is part of the Mughal-Rajput conflicts. Thus, the correct answer is Humayun because Bahadur Shah's attack on Chittor took place while Humayun was the Mughal emperor.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस मुग़ल बादशाह के शासनकाल में बहादुर शाह ने चित्तौड़ पर आक्रमण किया था? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)

शाहजहाँ
हुमायूँ

Explanation:
बहादुर शाह (गुजरात का सुल्तान) ने चित्तौड़ पर आक्रमण 1535 ई. में मुगल बादशाह हुमायूँ के शासनकाल में किया था। हुमायूँ (1530-1540 और 1555-1556) मुगल साम्राज्य के दूसरे शासक थे। इस समय चित्तौड़ पर राणा संग्राम सिंह (राणा सांगा) का शासन था, जिन्होंने बहादुर शाह के आक्रमण के खिलाफ मदद माँगी थी। हालाँकि, हुमायूँ ने चित्तौड़ पर हमला नहीं किया, बल्कि बहादुर शाह ने राणा सांगा से लोहा लिया। बाद में हुमायूँ ने बहादुर शाह को हराकर गुजरात पर अधिकार किया। चित्तौड़ का युद्ध मुगलों और राजपूतों के बीच संघर्ष का हिस्सा था, पर प्रश्न बहादुर शाह के आक्रमण से संबंधित है जो हुमायूँ के शासनकाल में हुआ।

question: Match the following Rulers with their titles correctly. Set – I Set - II a. Tarikh-i-Sindh 1. Nizamuddin Bakshi b. Tarikh-i-Kashmir 2. Arif kandhari c. Tabaqat-i-Akbari 3. Mirza Massom d. Tarikh-i-Akbari 4. Mirza Haider (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: a -3; b - 4; c - 2; d - 1
a - 3; b - 4; c - 1; d - 2
a - 4; b - 3; c - 2; d - 1
a - 2; b - 3; c - 4; d - 1
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a - 3; b - 4; c - 1; d - 2

Explanation:
Tarikh-i-Sindh (a) is authored by Mirza Massom (3), dealing with the history of Sindh. Tarikh-i-Kashmir (b) is authored by Mirza Haider (4), covering the history of Kashmir. Tabaqat-i-Akbari (c) is written by Nizamuddin Bakshi (1), a detailed history of Akbar's reign. Tarikh-i-Akbari (d) is authored by Arif Kandhari (2), also about Akbar's period. These are important Mughal historical texts, and correct matching of authors is crucial for understanding sources of Mughal history.

question: The mother of Jahangir was a Kachhwaha princess, a daughter of Rajput ruler of ___________. (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Marwar
Amber
Mewar
Berar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Amber

Explanation:
The mother of Jahangir was Mariam-uz-Zamani, who was the daughter of Raja Bharmal (Bhagwandas), the Rajput ruler of Amber (present-day Jaipur). Raja Bharmal belonged to the Kachhwaha dynasty. Akbar sought an alliance with the Rajputs through matrimony, resulting in the marriage of his son Salim (later Jahangir) to the Kachhwaha princess. This marriage strengthened Mughal-Rajput relations and brought stability to the empire. Mariam-uz-Zamani was given high status in the Mughal court and influenced Jahangir's character with Hindu traditions. Thus, this relationship is a key example of Mughal-Rajput cooperation.

question: Who among the following was the successor of Sultan Iltutmish in Delhi Sultanate? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Alauddin Khilji
Feroz Tughlaq
Alptekin
Raziya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Raziya

Explanation:
Sultan Iltutmish (r. 1211-1236 CE) of the Delhi Sultanate appointed his daughter Raziya as his successor during his lifetime, preferring her over his sons due to her competence. After Iltutmish's death in 1236 CE, Raziya ascended the throne and became the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling until 1240 CE. The other options are incorrect: Alauddin Khilji was a ruler of the Khilji dynasty (late 13th century), Feroz Tughlaq belonged to the Tughlaq dynasty (14th century), and Alptekin was a Ghaznavid general. Thus, Raziya is the correct successor.

question: Angkor Vat temple, which is dedicated to the god Vishnu, was built in the 12th century by __________, the king of Kambuja (Cambodia). (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Indravarman I
Yasovarman I
Jayavarman II
Surya Varman II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Surya Varman II

Explanation:
Angkor Wat temple, located in the Angkor region of Cambodia, is a massive Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu. It was built in the early 12th century by King Suryavarman II of the Khmer Empire. The construction took about 30 years and is a masterpiece of Khmer architecture. The walls are adorned with carvings depicting scenes from the Ramayana and the Mahabharata. Although originally a Hindu temple, it was later converted into a Buddhist temple. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is also depicted on the national flag of Cambodia.

question: In one of his famous works, Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi claims that the founder of _____ was a descendant of the Prophet. (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:
In his famous work 'Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi', Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi claims that the founder of the Sayyid Dynasty was a descendant of Prophet Muhammad. The Sayyid Dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1414 to 1451 CE. It was founded by Khizr Khan, who was initially appointed as governor by Timur and later declared independence. His successors claimed the title 'Sayyid' (descendant of the Prophet). The last ruler of this dynasty was Alam Shah, who was defeated by Bahlol Lodi, marking the beginning of the Lodi Dynasty. This claim is recorded in historical documents, though historians debate its authenticity.

question: The Chalukyas of Badami were founded by: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Kirttivarman I

Explanation:
The Chalukya dynasty of Badami was founded by Pulakesin I in the 6th century CE. He established Vatapi (modern Badami) as their capital and laid the foundation of the Chalukya empire. Pulakesin I performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice and assumed the title 'Maharajadhiraja'. His son Kirttivarman I succeeded him and expanded the kingdom. The most famous ruler of this dynasty was Pulakesin II, who defeated Harsha on the banks of the Narmada River. The Chalukyas were pioneers in art and architecture, as seen in the cave temples of Badami. The dynasty ruled for over two centuries and left a lasting impact on South Indian history.

question: Which of the following architectures has been built in the 'Charbagh' style? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (10/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Taj Mahal
Gumbaj of Bijapur
Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque
Qutub Minar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Taj Mahal

Explanation:
Charbagh style is a distinct Mughal architectural style where a garden is divided into four parts separated by pathways or water channels. This style was derived from Persian architecture. The Taj Mahal, built by Shah Jahan between 1632-1653 AD, is an excellent example of this style. The main tomb is not at the center but at the northern end near the Yamuna River, yet the garden is divided into four parts. The Gumbaj of Bijapur represents Deccan architecture, while the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and Qutub Minar reflect the architecture of the Delhi Sultanate period.

question: 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' in Ajmer was built in the period of which of the following dynasties? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 1)

question: The famous building 'Qutub Minar' has been built under which style of architecture? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Sharqi Style

Mughal Style
Seljuk Style
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mamulek Style

Explanation:
Qutub Minar is the tallest minaret in India, started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1193 and completed by Iltutmish. It is an excellent example of the Mamulek (Slave Dynasty) style of architecture. This style uses red sandstone and marble, featuring Islamic calligraphy and Quranic verses. The balconies are adorned with muqarnas (honeycomb vaulting), a hallmark of this style. The Mamulek style laid the foundation of Turkish architecture in India, which later evolved into the Mughal style. The structure is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993.

'गुलाम वंश' (स्लेव डायनेस्टी) भारत में दिल्ली सल्तनत का पहला राजवंश था, जिसकी स्थापना 1206 ई. में कुतुब-उद-दीन ऐबक ने की थी। वह मोहम्मद गोरी का गुलाम था, लेकिन बाद में स्वतंत्र शासक बन गया। इस वंश का नाम इसलिए पड़ा क्योंकि इसके अधिकांश शासक गुलाम थे या गुलामों के वंशज थे। कुतुब-उद-दीन ऐबक ने दिल्ली में कुव्वत-उल-इस्लाम मस्जिद और कुतुब मीनार का निर्माण शुरू करवाया। उसका शासनकाल 1206 से 1210 ई. तक रहा। उसकी मृत्यु के बाद इल्तुतमिश गद्दी पर बैठा।
